test.title: guest can add a product to the cart
test.error:
Error: expect(locator).toBeVisible() failed
Locator: getByText('Product added to shopping cart.')
Expected: visible

triage.reason: The failure is deterministic (3/3 attempts, same "element(s) not found"), which rules out flakiness. The steps before the assertion succeeded: the product heading click and the "Add to cart" button click both resolved, so the page and the add-to-cart control are present and actionable. Only the hard-coded confirmation string failed to match anything in the DOM, which most likely means the toast/alert copy no longer equals 'Product added to shopping cart.' (e.g. punctuation or wording drift) or is rendered in a node the text locator doesn't reach. The alternative — add-to-cart silently failing so no confirmation is shown (real bug) — cannot be excluded, but there is no screenshot, trace, or failed cart API in the evidence to support it, and a locator matching nothing by default indicates the page or locator changed.
triage.evidence: "Locator: getByText('Product added to shopping cart.') / Expected: visible / Error: element(s) not found" while the preceding line `await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Add to cart' }).click();` completed without error, and the test "failed on every attempt (3 attempts)".
triage.next_step: Re-run with `--trace on` and open the trace's DOM snapshot for the step right after the "Add to cart" click: read the actual toast/alert text and update the locator (e.g. `page.getByRole('alert')` or `getByText(/added to .*cart/i)`); if the snapshot shows no confirmation at all and the cart stays empty / the cart API call fails, reclassify as a real bug.

triage.reason: Deterministic failure (3/3 attempts) where the locator matched nothing at all — "element(s) not found" rather than hidden or multiple matches — so timing/state is ruled out. The failure rests on two unverified test-side assumptions, both of which produce exactly this symptom: (1) the hard-coded sentence 'There are no products found.' may not be the app's actual empty-state wording (getByText does normalized substring matching, so a shorter real message like 'No products found.' yields zero matches), and (2) the mock pattern '**/products' matches against the full URL including query string, so a real request such as /api/products?page=1 would never be intercepted, letting real products render with no empty state. No evidence in the report establishes that the app is required to render that exact string, so per standard triage a zero-match locator defaults to a locator/expected-value mismatch. A genuinely missing empty state in the app is the competing possibility, which keeps this at medium rather than high confidence.
triage.evidence: Error line: "Locator: getByText('There are no products found.') ... Error: element(s) not found". Code line: "await page.route('**/products', (route) => route.fulfill({ status: 200, json: { data: [] } }));" — the glob ends at 'products' and is matched against the full URL including any query string.
triage.next_step: Re-run with tracing on and open the trace's Network tab to confirm whether the '**/products' route actually intercepted the request (if the real URL carries a query string, widen the pattern to '**/products*' or a regex); then grep the product-list component for the real empty-state string and align the assertion text with it.

triage.reason: The test waits for a response whose request method is the non-standard HTTP verb 'QUERY'. A category filter on a product list is normally fetched with GET (or POST) /products?..., so the predicate can never match and waitForResponse times out. The failure repeated on all 3 attempts at the same line, which rules out flakiness, and the listener is correctly registered before the checkbox click, so the only wrong element is the test's expectation about the request method. Less likely alternative: the app fires no request at all when the filter is checked (real bug), which cannot be fully excluded without a network log.
triage.evidence: "Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded." with predicate `(response) => response.request().method() === 'QUERY' && response.url().endsWith('/products')`
triage.next_step: Open the shop in a browser with DevTools → Network, tick the "Pliers" category filter, and read the actual method/URL of the products request; then fix the predicate (likely `method() === 'GET'` and `url().includes('/products')` to allow query strings).

test.title: Combining a category and a brand shows only products matching both

Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.
Error: page.waitForResponse: Test timeout of 30000ms exceeded.

triage.reason: The timeout is on the test's own response matcher, not on an app action. The predicate requires the request method to be the exotic/experimental 'QUERY' verb and the URL to end exactly with '/products'; a filter request from this shop is a GET and carries query parameters, so the URL would not end with '/products' either. The predicate therefore can never match, which explains an identical failure on all 3 attempts. The page itself loaded (first product name was visible) and the category filter locator resolved and was checked without error, so there is no evidence of app breakage. Less likely alternative: the app fires no request on check at all, but that would require the predicate's method and URL shape to be coincidentally right.
